v1.kill_reason: Exact integer ranks are not deterministically gradable against a fair spec: network-simplex optima are non-unique, so the graphviz binary's pivot order and tie-breaks decide the output. A different valid optimal ranking would fail, which violates the acceptance-breadth rule. Fix options: restrict rank grading to uniquely-optimal graphs or drop ranks, then resubmit. The parser and -Tcanon/-Tdot buckets are the viable core.

spike_plan.kill_if: Ranks change under equivalent statement reordering for a meaningful share of graphs, or -Tcanon/-Tdot output is non-deterministic across runs.
spike_plan.pass_if: Output is deterministic across runs and the parser/canonical buckets are byte-stable under statement reordering, while any rank variation is confined to a small, identifiable set of graphs.
steps: In a throwaway networked Debian container, clone gitlab.com/graphviz/graphviz at tag 16.1.0 (not 644fa57) and build dot; confirm the built binary matches apt graphviz output.
Run dot -Tcanon and dot -Tdot over the tests/graphs corpus three times; confirm byte-identical output (determinism) and count the files (checks the 265 claim).

Take 30 corpus graphs that have rank ties and shuffle statement order (keeping semantics); rerun dot -Tdot and compare ranks. Any rank change means graphviz ranks are not a unique function of the graph.
Hand-write ten small DOT cases that exercise default attribute scoping inside subgraphs and edge-chain expansion; check -Tcanon output by hand against the binary.
Record which of the parser, canonical output and rank buckets are deterministic on the oracle side.

v1.summary: Graphviz is real (EPL-2.0, 16.1.0 released 4 Sep 2026, commit 644fa57 unverified) with a strong byte-exact oracle, and public Rust DOT parsers cover only the parsing slice. The card is killed under K4 because exact integer ranks depend on graphviz's non-unique network-simplex tie-breaks, so a valid alternative ranking would fail; a resubmission restricted to parser and canonical output, or to uniquely-optimal ranks, would be worth re-validating.
